text:
Jia Chen: Heads up — we're onboarding Sigma's customer adapter (LoRA) to base v1.2.0. They want 4-bit quant support and retain instruction-following. Can someone run a quick compatibility + quality pack?
Arpit Rao: I pulled their adapter and attempted a straight merge with our merge script. hit a key namespace mismatch, patched locally. command I ran: `python tools/merge_lora.py --base models/1.2.0 --adapter uploads/sigma_v1 --out merges/sigma_v1_merged`
Arpit Rao: Error snippet: 
```
KeyError: 'module.base_model.model.decoder.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.weight'
```
Arpit Rao: Fixed by applying a small rename map on load: `--rename 'module.base_model.' ''` and re-serializing. no weight size mismatches after that.
Sara Lopez: Can we run the quick eval pack focused on: instruction-following (LLM-suite prompts), refusal cases, numeric/math, and a small safety checklist? I can run it on a small GPU node.
Miguel Torres: ran quickpack on 4-bit quantized merged model (q4_0). summary: 52 tests total, 48 pass. instruction-follow accuracy 88% -> baseline 92% (delta -4pts). ROUGE-L down ~2.3. Hallucination flag rate 1.2% -> 2.0%.
Miguel Torres: command: `python eval/quickpack.py --model merges/sigma_v1_merged --quant q4_0 --out reports/sigma_quick_171995`
eval-bot: quickpack finished: 48/52 tests passed. failing tests: numeric_accuracy, date-parsing, long-context-truncation. artifacts: https://redwood-internal/reports/sigma_quick_171995
Kevin Park: Slight regression on instruction-following — is it due to adapter or quantization? did you run a float32 eval?
Miguel Torres: yes, float32 merged model retains 91% instr-follow (baseline 92%). so ~1pt loss from adapter, +3pts from quant. ordering looks additive.
Arpit Rao: there was also a small change in tokenization during client's finetune (they used an extra special token). loader ignored it by default which shifts embeddings for that token. I re-inserted the token mapping with `--force-token-map uploads/sigma_v1/tokens.json` and re-ran merge, slight improvement in numeric prompts.
Sara Lopez: good catch. I'll add a couple customer-specific prompt pairs to the quickpack focusing on dates and arithmetic.
Jia Chen: Proposed plan: (1) run full eval on dedicated infra (all eval suites + safety) (2) if regressions >3% on any category, request customer do a quant-aware adapter finetune or we do a small post-merge calibration (3) canary deploy to 5% traffic behind routing policy + rollback if errors >1% or latency >SLO.
Kevin Park: also want perf measurements — 4-bit path sometimes changes KV cache behavior. check median latency and p95.
Miguel Torres: perf rough numbers tomorrow: expected median +0.8ms, p95 +6ms on our batch sizes. will run batching matrix: [1,4,8] and prefix cache enabled/disabled.
Jia Chen: I'll schedule the canary for Tue and collect sign-off from customer for the change log. Sara — can you assemble the quickpack diffs and add them to the report?
Sara Lopez: on it, will attach failing examples and short repro steps. :thumbsup:
Arpit Rao: note for ops: merge artifact stored at `s3://redwood-artifacts/merges/sigma_v1_merged/` and model-card draft at https://redwood-internal/model-cards/sigma_v1_merged.md
eval-bot: canary scheduled: Tue 09:00 UTC (5% traffic). will emit rollout events.
Jia Chen: thanks team — keep thread for updates. ping me if any new blockers. :eyes:
